title: Descent of a pointed smooth family and invertible integer to one stage
statement: Let $I$ be a small cofiltered category, $X:I\to\mathrm{Scheme}$ a diagram with affine transition maps and Noetherian quasi-separated stages [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and $\alpha:S\to X$ a limiting cone. Let $c:C\to S$ be quasi-compact, quasi-separated, smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and geometrically connected, with a section $\sigma:S\to C$, and let $n\in\mathbf N$ be invertible in $\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S)$. There exist $i\in I$, a scheme $P$, morphisms $p:P\to X_i$, $\tau:X_i\to P$, and $a:C\to P$ such that $(c,a,\alpha_i,p)$ is a pullback [def-pc-fibre-product], $\sigma a=\alpha_i\tau$, and $\tau p=1_{X_i}$. The morphism $p$ is quasi-compact, quasi-separated, smooth and geometrically connected, and $n$ is invertible in $\Gamma(X_i,\mathcal O_{X_i})$.

proof.text: First descend an inverse to n using global-section continuity. Descend the equation n*t=1 by zero-equality descent for n*t-1. Restrict to Over k at the resulting unit stage; every subsequent stage still has n invertible by functoriality of global sections.
Descend the qcqs smooth family by finite-presentation descent. Apply eventual smoothness for arbitrary affine-transition systems to its model and pass to that later pullback.

Apply fixed-stage map descent to the section composed with the comparison into the smooth model. Pull back the model to that refinement and construct the section as the pullback lift of the descended map and the identity. Its section equation is the second projection identity, and compatibility follows from both projection identities. No separate equality-descent step is needed.

Take the open section component from the smooth section-component theorem. The image under the comparison of a connected original fibre is preconnected and contains the image of its section, hence lies in the model fibre component through its section. Lift both the comparison and section through the open. Prove the restricted square cartesian by its universal property and cancellation against the open immersion. The smooth finitely presented model over a Noetherian stage is Noetherian; hence its open has a Noetherian underlying space, making its structural map quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Geometric irreducibility of the open gives geometric connectedness. Read its index back in I and transport the stage unit along the transition map.

theorem exists_pointed_smooth_family_stage {I : Type u} [SmallCategory I]
    [IsCofiltered I] {S C : Scheme.{u}}
    (X : I ⥤ Scheme.{u}) (α : (Functor.const I).obj S ⟶ X)
    (hα : IsLimit (Cone.mk S α))
    (hXa : ∀ {i j : I} (f : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (X.map f))
    (hN : ∀ i, IsNoetherian (X.obj i))
    (hqs : ∀ i, QuasiSeparatedSpace (X.obj i))
    (c : C ⟶ S) [QuasiCompact c] [QuasiSeparated c] [Smooth c] [GeometricallyConnected c]
    (σ : S ⟶ C) (hσ : σ ≫ c = 𝟙 S) (n : ℕ) (hn : IsUnit (n : Γ(S, ⊤))) :
    ∃ (i : I) (P : Scheme.{u}) (p : P ⟶ X.obj i) (τ : X.obj i ⟶ P) (a : C ⟶ P),
      IsPullback c a (α.app i) p ∧ σ ≫ a = α.app i ≫ τ ∧
      QuasiCompact p ∧ QuasiSeparated p ∧ Smooth p ∧ GeometricallyConnected p ∧
      τ ≫ p = 𝟙 (X.obj i) ∧ IsUnit (n : Γ(X.obj i, ⊤))
